post.caption:
The cornea does most of the refraction, the lens fine-tunes it, and the image lands upside down on the retina. Where the optic nerve leaves there are no photoreceptors at all, so each eye has a genuine blind spot you never notice, because your brain fills it with plausible surroundings. Short and long sight are just the eyeball being slightly the wrong length, and glasses move the focal point back onto the retina.
